name: Adenovirus Infection in Immunocompromised Patients

criteria.description: Detection of adenovirus DNA or antigen in blood, tissue, or body fluids by PCR or immunohistochemistry
Presence of clinical signs consistent with adenovirus infection such as hemorrhagic cystitis, pneumonia, or gastroenteritis in an immunocompromised host
Exclusion of other infectious etiologies that could explain clinical presentation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of adenovirus by molecular or antigen testing in an immunocompromised patient with compatible clinical symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on molecular detection methods due to nonspecific clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic in bone marrow transplant recipients

common.notes: Though hepatic is not in valid body systems, this can be considered under constitutional or omitted
searchTerms: high liver enzymes showing liver inflammation
signs of hepatitis in blood tests
liver injury indicated by enzyme elevation

rare.symptomName: Severe disseminated adenoviral infection with multi-organ failure

laboratory: Positive adenovirus PCR in blood, urine, respiratory secretions, or tissue samples
imaging: Chest radiograph or CT showing bilateral interstitial infiltrates in adenoviral pneumonia
other: Histopathological evidence of adenoviral inclusions in biopsy specimens
Detection of adenoviral antigen by immunohistochemistry

distinguishingFeatures: CMV often presents with retinitis and colitis rather than hemorrhagic cystitis
CMV PCR positivity differentiates from adenovirus
BK virus primarily causes nephropathy and hemorrhagic cystitis but lacks respiratory symptoms
BK virus PCR positive, adenovirus PCR negative

redFlags: Severe hemorrhagic cystitis with urinary obstruction
Disseminated adenoviral infection with multi-organ dysfunction
references: Lion T. Adenovirus infections in immunocompetent and immunocompromised patients. Clin Microbiol Rev. 2014 Apr;27(3):441-62.
Echavarria M. Adenoviruses in immunocompromised hosts. Clin Microbiol Rev. 2008 Oct;21(4):704-15.
Chakrabarti S, et al. Adenovirus infection in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients: risk factors, natural history, and outcome. Blood. 2002 Mar 15;99(6):1981-8.
